provider: Kaggle Notebook outputs (/kaggle/working) — the free side-channel

free_tier.stated: Up to 20 GB of output per notebook version saved to /kaggle/working, and every 'Save & Run All' creates a new version. Outputs are themselves addable as dataset inputs to any future notebook. No documented cap on the number of notebook versions or notebooks per account.

retention.stated: | Outputs persist indefinitely and are downloadable years later; the flaky part is the commit step (a timed-out run loses the output).

egress.terms: Free download of notebook output files from the version's Output tab, same GCS-backed delivery.

tooling: kaggle CLI (`kaggle kernels output <owner>/<kernel> -p ./dir`) and kagglehub; the notebook itself runs on free P100/TPU compute so the write happens server-side with no upload from the client at all.
chaining: 20 GB per notebook version. Notebook versions, notebooks and accounts each carry no stated limit. The reachable total therefore scales with versions and notebooks per account, and a second account carries a second allowance. The whole write path is server-side (the data is produced or fetched inside the notebook, so there is no client uplink bottleneck). This is the standard community alternative route around the 200 GB private quota: a Kaggle forum answer describes it as 'create a new notebook from your dataset and copy files to /kaggle/working'.
limits_note: 20 GB per version is hard; 9 h / 12 h session limits per run; output is only persisted on commit ('Save & Run All'), not on interactive save; GPU/TPU hours are rationed (~30 h/week) but CPU-only runs are not the constraint for pure storage.
reliability_note: Outputs persist indefinitely and are downloadable years later; the flaky part is the commit step (a timed-out run loses the output).
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.
